title: Sign-in screen crashed on load
symptom: Every role except the bare sign-in page failed. The page rendered the banner and then stopped, with no form at all.
root_cause: The role selector was given an on_change callback while inside an st.form. Streamlit forbids callbacks on widgets inside a form (StreamlitInvalidFormCallbackError), so the whole page aborted.
fix: Moved the role selector outside the form and keyed the login and password fields by role, which achieves the same behaviour without a callback: switching role offers that role's demonstration account.
verification: B02, B03, B04, B05, B06 all pass; the sign-in form renders for every role.

title: Timetable slots did not block a new reservation
symptom: A room shown as free by the search could still carry a timetabled class, and the insert then failed with a generic database refusal.
root_cause: Availability united all three occupancy sources, but the create path only checked live reservations. The exclusion trigger correctly refused, but the caller was told nothing useful and got no alternatives.
fix: The create path now checks the timetable explicitly and returns TIMETABLE_OCCUPIED with three ranked alternatives, matching how it already handled reservations.
verification: TC-61 and TC-73 pass; booking a timetabled room now yields TIMETABLE_OCCUPIED with alternatives.

title: Internal database errors surfaced as the wrong code
symptom: A failed foreign key was reported as a generic DATABASE constraint, and a mistyped section code reached the engine instead of being caught.
root_cause: The create path did not validate the section reference, and the IntegrityError mapper only knew the three exclusion constraint names.
fix: Section codes are validated up front (INVALID_SECTION), and a foreign key failure is mapped to REFERENCE_MISSING with a readable message.
verification: TC-116 passes; a nonexistent section is refused with INVALID_SECTION before any insert.

title: Audit replay declared a booked room free
symptom: Replaying a room's state at the start of a reservation reported no occupation.
root_cause: The replay asked whether the instant overlapped the interval. An instant is not an interval: with a half-open comparison a zero-length probe can never overlap, which defeated the check.
fix: The replay now tests containment, start <= at < end, which is the question being asked.
verification: TC-117 passes; a reservation created at the replay instant is reported as occupying the room, and after cancellation it is not.

title: Assistant guardrail could not be tested, and matched the word “to”
symptom: The hallucinated-room guardrail was inline in the ask() function, so it could not be exercised directly; and room codes were matched case-insensitively, so the office code TO matched the English word.
root_cause: No seam for the check, and one flag doing two jobs: parsing a question (ignore case) versus validating an answer (exact code).
fix: Extracted apply_guardrail() as a pure function and matched answer codes case-sensitively against bookable rooms only.
verification: TC-126 and TC-126b pass: a drafted answer naming a room outside the result set is replaced by the plain list; a clean answer passes through untouched. TC-129 asserts the module contains no write path.

title: Reserve heading shown with nothing to reserve
symptom: When no single room could seat a request, the page still printed the heading “Reserve one of these” above an empty list.
root_cause: The heading was emitted before the empty-options branch.
fix: The heading is now emitted only when there is something to reserve, and the empty case points at the split panel instead.
verification: B10 and B11 pass with the split panel and no orphan heading.

title: A reschedule of a pending reservation read as a new approval request
symptom: Moving a reservation that was waiting for approval produced the message “Request recorded for approval”, which describes a new request rather than a move.
root_cause: One renderer decided the wording from the resulting status alone, so every action on a pending row looked like a creation.
fix: render_result() now takes the action (created, moved, cancelled, released, approved, rejected, displaced) and chooses the wording from the action and the status together.
verification: B14 passes and reports “Moved, still waiting for approval”.

title: Audit screen crashed on rows with non-JSON state
symptom: Opening the Before-and-after panel raised a traceback and the screen replaced itself with an error.
root_cause: audit.diff() assumed both state columns were JSON objects; older and hand-written rows hold plain strings, and json.loads raised.
fix: States are coerced before diffing: a non-JSON value becomes a single named field, so the view degrades instead of failing.
verification: TC-141 passes and B32 passes; the panel renders for mixed row shapes.

title: Completed reservations disappeared from the record the student can see
symptom: Once a booking was automatically closed as COMPLETED, the student's schedule and the report picker no longer listed it, so a class that had already happened could not be reported as wrong.
root_cause: The section-schedule query listed four statuses and omitted COMPLETED.
fix: COMPLETED is included; the record of a finished class stays visible and reportable.
verification: B18, B19 and B20 pass; the report picker lists completed reservations.

title: Timetabled classes were not counted as the student's next class
symptom: The student screen reported no upcoming class even though the timetable had one, because only reservations counted as live.
root_cause: The live filter in the student view excluded the TIMETABLE pseudo-status.
fix: TIMETABLE is treated as a live entry for the student's own schedule.
verification: B18 passes and the next-class callout names the timetabled class, room and time.

title: Closure results were rendered as a failed booking
symptom: A saved closure produced a success message followed by an empty failure block, because the shared renderer expected a booking payload.
root_cause: render_result() assumed every successful payload carried a booking.
fix: The renderer recognises a closure payload and a report payload and reports each in its own terms.
verification: B29 passes and reports the closure with the count of reservations that were inside it.

title: Confirming an inferred room fact silently did nothing
symptom: The confirm action returned success but the unconfirmed flag stayed set.
root_cause: unconfirmed was missing from the list of editable fields, so the update was filtered out before it reached the statement.
verification: TC-102 and B27 pass; the flag clears and the change is audited.

title: Deprecated table width argument
found_by: Application log during the browser run
symptom: Every table raised a deprecation warning and would break after the removal date.
fix: Replaced with width="stretch" throughout the interface layer.
verification: The warning is absent from the application log; the tables still stretch.

title: Demonstration accounts were all reachable from one password
found_by: Test design review (noting a deliberate prototype limitation)
symptom: Authentication is a fixed password per role, chosen so a reviewer can try all three.
root_cause: This is a prototype: the accounts are printed on the sign-in page on purpose, as the definition of done asks.
fix: Not a defect. Recorded so it is not mistaken for one. The policy layer, not the login, is what enforces role restrictions, and TC-16 to TC-33 assert every negative cell.
verification: Section 5.4 of the design says the refusal at the route is the security; the matrix tests assert it.
